draft.title: Ancient Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander histories
card: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have lived in Australia for more than 65,000 years. Their cultures are among the oldest continuing cultures in the world.
Sites hold physical evidence of past lives. Lake Mungo, on Paakantyi, Mutthi Mutthi and Ngiyampaa Country in New South Wales, has ancient human remains and campfire sites.
Stories, songs and law are passed down through generations. Some describe past events, such as changes in coastlines and landscapes, so they are a source of knowledge about the ancient past.
Historians can use both kinds of evidence together. Sites show what was left behind, and oral traditions record knowledge held by the people themselves.
draft.remember: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have lived here for more than 65,000 years, and sites and oral traditions both tell us about it.

a.q: Which statement best describes the history of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples in Australia?
opts: They have lived here for more than 65,000 years
They have lived here for about 5,000 years
They arrived here only after the first sea voyages
They have lived here for about 20,000 years
a.why: The evidence shows Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have lived in Australia for more than 65,000 years. The other options give much shorter times, which do not match the evidence from sites and oral traditions.
a.clue: Think about how many tens of thousands of years the evidence covers.

b.q: A student says that oral traditions are not real evidence because they were not written down. Which reply is best?
opts: Oral traditions pass knowledge down and are a source
Oral traditions only count if a site also proves them
Oral traditions are less reliable than sites like Lake Mungo
Oral traditions are just entertaining stories, not history
b.why: Oral traditions are passed down through generations and are a source of knowledge about the ancient past, so a source does not need to be written. The tempting wrong option says a site must prove them first, but the card treats both as sources that can be used together.
b.clue: Does a source have to be written to count as evidence?
